search-index.title: Build once, query many times
search-index.summary: After an upload or edit, extracted text updates the index. Search requests read that stored index and check access before ranking results.
search-index.note: The exercise calls the builder synchronously, so its caller waits for the writes. Normal application startup opens the existing index; it does not rebuild it. An update replaces one document’s entries, a deletion removes them, and changed word-splitting rules require a rebuild. Before returning content, search must check current permissions.

graph.title: Index build and query flow
graph.description: Source documents are split into words and written to a stored search index. A search reads the word-to-document entries for its query. Each matching document passes an access check before readable matches are scored, sorted and limited.

labels.text: The search path performs no index writes.

async.title: If indexing runs in the background
async.note: The search store must compare versions and write as one atomic operation: accept newer versions, ignore identical retries and reject conflicting content at the same version. Keep the version after deletion too. If worker v5 pauses while v6 finishes, its later write is rejected. A separate source-version check cannot guarantee this. Background processing makes search temporarily stale.

graph.title: Asynchronous index update
graph.description: An upload or edit is converted to text, placed on a durable queue, and applied to the stored index by a background worker. Searches use the previous index until the update finishes.

version-guard.title: Accept, ignore or reject an incoming revision
version-guard.summary: Compare the incoming source revision with the stored revision before changing current state.
version-guard.note: The source revision orders changes for one document. Production storage must make the comparison and write atomic.

graph.title: Revision-guarded update flow
graph.description: A newer change updates current state, an older or exact duplicate is ignored, and conflicting content at the same revision is rejected.

bounded-fanout.title: Bound downstream work and handle an ending request
bounded-fanout.summary: Cap active calls and keep ownership of each child operation while results, the request deadline, and caller cancellation can race.
bounded-fanout.note: After stopping pending work, apply the lesson’s contract: return allowed partial results, report a timeout, or propagate caller cancellation.

graph.title: Bounded downstream calls and request lifetime
graph.description: A request starts a bounded set of downstream calls. Completed calls enter a result collector while the caller and deadline remain active. If required work completes, the service builds its response. If the caller cancels or the deadline expires first, the service cancels and awaits pending calls, then follows the lesson’s partial-result, timeout, or cancellation contract.

rag-context.title: Keep search, model-input selection and answering distinct
rag-context.summary: Documents are split into searchable sections before a request. Each question retrieves permitted evidence, fits it into a size limit and preserves citations.
rag-context.note: Documents are split and indexed when source content changes. Search and model-input selection happen for each question. Each exercise implements only the stage named in its contract.

graph.title: Search and grounded-answer flow
graph.description: Documents are split into sections and indexed when they change. A query finds matching sections. Sections not allowed for this user are excluded. Readable evidence is selected within the model input limit and produces either a cited answer or a no-evidence response.

durable-ingestion.title: Make background index updates recoverable
durable-ingestion.summary: Commit the source change and a durable work record together, then let a worker update the search index.
durable-ingestion.note: At the search store, compare versions and write atomically. Accept only newer versions; identical retries do nothing. Retain deletion versions so an older job cannot restore removed content.

graph.title: Durable ingestion and indexing flow
graph.description: A connector change is stored with a pending-work record. A relay queues the work. A worker extracts and splits content. The search store atomically compares versions and accepts newer updates. Failures return to retry or reconciliation.

large-import.title: Large upload and background search flow
large-import.summary: The API owns upload authorization and status. Clients send bytes to original storage; verified completion schedules extraction and indexing. Queries read derived text with current access checks.
large-import.note: The diagram is an architecture proposal. Coding exercises implement local transfer, batch scheduling and UTF-8 extraction. The supplied SQLite demo uses one transaction per revision; it does not implement cloud sessions, queues, OCR or production staging. For download-only storage, omit the extraction/index branch. Reconcile completed objects missing metadata, and expire abandoned parts.

graph.title: Byte transfer, durable work and the query path
graph.description: A client requests a scoped upload session from the API and transfers parts to original storage. The API verifies completed storage and commits metadata with pending work. Workers consume pending jobs and read original bytes, then update the search index. Queries combine index matches with current authorization in metadata before returning content.
